Span
SPAN
n.
Old English spann, the distance between the outstretched thumb and little finger of a man’s hand (approximately 9 inches / 23 cm); a Hebrew small-linear-measure equal to half a cubit. Hebrew zēreth.

📖 Biblical Definition

The span is the small Hebrew linear measure equal to half a cubit (approximately 9 inches / 23 cm)—the distance between the outstretched thumb and little finger of a man’s hand when the palm is spread. Several biblical uses anchor the doctrine. First, the literal: Exodus 28:16 and 39:9 prescribe the breastplate of judgment as foursquare and doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof—a 9-inch square doubled to make a pouch holding the Urim and Thummim. The span is the precise dimension of the high priest’s breastplate. 1 Samuel 17:4 records the height of Goliath as six cubits and a span—approximately 9 feet 9 inches (depending on which cubit-standard is used), specifying the giant’s exact stature in the most easily-visualized small unit. The literal uses establish the span as a familiar everyday measurement, the hand-spread distance that any Israelite could verify against his own hand. Second, the figurative-prophetic. Isaiah 40:12 is the great use: who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance? The rhetorical question sets the LORD’s incomparable greatness against human smallness: the LORD measures the heavens themselves with a span—the same 9-inch hand-spread by which the Israelite measured his garment-cloth, applied by the divine hand to the very dimensions of the heavens. The figure is one of Scripture’s most striking expressions of God’s incomparable greatness; the smallness of the everyday human span is contrasted with the greatness of the God to whom even the heavens are span-measurable. Third, the human-life-brevity register. Psalm 39:5 (David’s great psalm of human frailty): behold, thou hast made my days as an handbreadth; and mine age is as nothing before thee: verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity. The handbreadth (a smaller unit than the span; approximately 3 inches) and the span here function as figures of the brevity of human life from the divine perspective. The believer’s life, measured against eternity, is a handbreadth—a span at most. The figure invites the saint to number his days, to apply his heart to wisdom, and to live with eternity in view rather than to be deceived by the apparent largeness of the span-length of his present life. The span as a biblical unit therefore serves both literal (architectural and bodily measurements) and figurative (the LORD’s greatness, the brevity of life) functions; its everyday-familiarity makes it a particularly effective vehicle for both kinds of biblical teaching.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines SPAN as the space from the end of the thumb to the end of the little finger, when extended; nine inches; the eighth of a fathom; in scripture, both a literal small-linear-measure (Goliath’s height, the high priest’s breastplate) and figuratively the standard by which God measures the heavens (Isa 40:12) and by which the brevity of human life is conveyed (Ps 39:5).

SPAN, n. — The space from the end of the thumb to the end of the little finger, when extended; the eighth of a fathom; nine inches.

HANDBREADTH, n. — A measure of three or four inches; the breadth of the hand; used figuratively in Ps 39:5 of the brevity of human life.

📖 Key Scripture

Isaiah 40:12 — "Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?"

Psalm 39:5 — "Behold, thou hast made my days as an handbreadth; and mine age is as nothing before thee: verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity."

1 Samuel 17:4 — "And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span."

Exodus 28:16 — "Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The span as a biblical unit is corrupted in modern reading chiefly by being converted to inches and skipped past, losing the rhetorical force of Isaiah 40:12’s contrast (the same span by which men measure cloth is the unit by which God measures heaven) and the pastoral weight of Psalm 39:5’s handbreadth-image of life’s brevity.

expand to see more

Modern conversion of biblical measurements into inches-and-centimeters often muffles the rhetorical force the biblical writers built into their figures. Isaiah 40:12’s use of span is one of the most striking examples. The Israelite hearer knew the span: it was the everyday measurement he used for cloth, for room-dimensions, for the small distances of daily life. To hear that the LORD meted out heaven with the span—the same span the hearer used for ordinary measurements—was to encounter the incomparable greatness of God in a register the smallest household economy could vividly grasp. The modern translation that converts span to handbreadths or to 9-inch units loses the immediate connection to the hearer’s own hand-spread. The recovery is the recovery of the figure: the same hand-distance by which the saint measures his garment is the unit by which God measures heaven; the smallness of the human span against the greatness of the divine application sets the LORD’s incomparable greatness in sharpest relief.

Psalm 39:5’s use of the handbreadth carries similar pastoral substance. Behold, thou hast made my days as an handbreadth—David measures the length of his life against the smallest familiar unit, and finds that his days, even at his best state, are as nothing before God. The figure is meant to produce the wisdom-effect of Psalm 90:12: so teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom. The contemporary believer who lives as if the span-length of his present life were a large amount of time has missed the perspective the handbreadth-figure intends to teach. The recovery is the recovery of the figure’s force: my life, measured against eternity, is a handbreadth; my best years are a span; the soberness of this measurement should drive me to apply my heart to wisdom while the brief span remains. The span and handbreadth as biblical units are therefore not chiefly numismatic or architectural curiosities but the vivid figures by which Scripture teaches both the greatness of God and the brevity of life—each in the smallest unit the everyday hand provides.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew zēreth (span); a small linear measure (half a cubit, approximately 9 inches); used literally for the high priest’s breastplate and Goliath’s height, and figuratively for the LORD’s span-measurement of heaven (Isa 40:12) and the handbreadth-brevity of human life (Ps 39:5).

expand to see more

Hebrew zēreth (H2239) — span (7 OT uses; Ex 28:16; 39:9; 1 Sam 17:4; Isa 40:12; Ezek 43:13).

Hebrew tōphach / tephach (H2947, H2948) — handbreadth (a smaller unit, approximately 3 inches; Ex 25:25; 1 Kgs 7:26; Ps 39:5).

Hebrew ’ammāh (H520) — cubit (the larger linear unit; 2 spans make 1 cubit).

Hebrew zēreth-cognates in Akkadian and other Semitic languages — the span as a widespread ancient-Near-Eastern unit based on the hand-spread.

Usage

"Meted out heaven with the span—Isa 40:12’s incomparable-greatness figure: the same hand-distance by which men measure cloth is the unit by which God measures the heavens."

"Thou hast made my days as an handbreadth—Ps 39:5’s pastoral figure of life’s brevity, measured against eternity."

"Modern conversion to inches loses the rhetorical force; recovery is the figure in its everyday-familiarity: the span is the hand-spread the hearer himself uses, and its application to heaven and to human life carries the substantive force the biblical writers intended."
